title: WPS Office vs Excel: Which Should You Use?
dek: WPS Spreadsheet is a free, Excel-like desktop app with strong .xlsx compatibility; Excel is the paid industry standard with deeper features. WPS covers everyday work at no cost, Excel wins on power and macros. Here is how they compare.

seo.metaTitle: WPS Office vs Excel: Which Should You Use?
seo.metaDescription: WPS Office vs Excel compared: a free, Excel-like spreadsheet versus the paid standard. Cost, features, .xlsx compatibility, ads, and who each is for.

richText: WPS Spreadsheet and Microsoft Excel do the same core job — rows, columns, and formulas — but they sit at opposite ends of the price scale. WPS is free and built to look and feel almost exactly like Excel; Excel is a paid subscription and the standard most workplaces run on. The right pick depends on your budget, the features you actually need, and how often you trade files with Excel users.

body.caption: WPS Spreadsheet vs Excel at a glance

richText: Choose Excel when you need the deepest features or when compatibility is non-negotiable. Its advanced tools — Power Query, full VBA macros, richer charting, and the widest set of functions — are ahead of WPS, and it stays fast with very large datasets. If your workplace or clients send complex, macro-heavy .xlsx files, Excel opens them exactly as intended, every time.

Choose WPS Spreadsheet when you want a capable, familiar spreadsheet without paying. Its interface is so close to Excel that most people feel at home instantly, its .xlsx support is strong, and it runs on nearly every platform — including Linux, Android, and iOS. body.richText: The main catches with the free version are ads and a few gaps. WPS shows ads and puts some tools (like advanced PDF features) behind its Premium tier, and very complex Excel macros or VBA may not carry over perfectly. If you rely on heavy macros, test a few files before committing.

body.text: Cost and compatibility: the deciding factors

richText: For most people, the choice comes down to two things: cost and files. If you rarely share spreadsheets, or share simple ones, WPS gives you an Excel-like experience for free and you skip the subscription. If you live in a world of complex, macro-heavy Excel files that must look and behave identically for everyone, Excel is the safer choice — and worth the cost.

items: WPS Spreadsheet is not ideal for teams that depend on full VBA, Power Query, or guaranteed formatting fidelity with complex .xlsx files — or for anyone who finds the ads distracting.

items.question: Is WPS Office as good as Excel?
items.answerRichText: For everyday work — budgets, lists, calculations, common formulas — it is very close, and it is free with an almost identical interface. Excel pulls ahead on advanced features like Power Query, full VBA macros, very large datasets, and perfect compatibility with complex .xlsx files.

items.question: Can WPS Office open Excel files?
items.answerRichText: Yes. WPS opens and saves .xlsx files natively, so you can work with Excel documents directly. Simple files transfer perfectly; very complex macros or advanced formatting may not carry over exactly, so test important files first.

items.question: Is WPS Office really free?
items.answerRichText: The core WPS Office is free to download and use, including the spreadsheet app. It is supported by ads, and a paid Premium tier removes them and unlocks extras like advanced PDF tools and more cloud storage.

items.question: Is WPS Office safe to use?
items.answerRichText: WPS Office is a widely used suite from Kingsoft with hundreds of millions of users. As with any free software, download it only from the official WPS website, and review the privacy settings during setup if you prefer to limit data sharing.
